intro.headline: Connecting the border to Tebrau
intro.body: The RTS Link from Woodlands lands at Bukit Chagar. Two concept E-ART lines could take it from there: north to Ulu Tiram and west to Bukit Indah.

tour.title: Across the strait
tour.body: The RTS Link crosses the strait from Woodlands North and lands at Bukit Chagar. This is where both concept E-ART lines begin.

fact.text: The RTS Link is a 4 km rail shuttle to Woodlands North. Over the middle of the Straits of Johor, its viaduct stands 25 m above the water.

tour.title: One interchange, three ways out
tour.body: JB Sentral (KTM and buses), the CIQ checkpoint, City Square and Komtar JBCC all sit within a short walk of Bukit Chagar.

tour.title: The old town and the waterfront
tour.body: The Iskandar Puteri line heads west past the Sultan Abu Bakar Mosque, Dataran Bandaraya and Hospital Sultanah Aminah.

fact.text: Tourism Johor lists the Sultan Abu Bakar Mosque as the earliest mosque in Johor Bahru, built in 1892.

tour.title: Danga Bay
tour.body: The coastal stretch: a string of waterfront towers along the Iskandar Puteri line.

tour.title: To Bukit Indah
tour.body: The Iskandar Puteri line ends at Bukit Indah, about 15 km from Bukit Chagar. Puteri Harbour and Legoland are further south and are not on this concept line.

fact.text: Legoland Malaysia, south of here, opened in September 2012 as Asia's first Legoland theme park.

tour.title: Up the Tebrau spine
tour.body: The Tebrau line runs north on Jalan Tebrau past Plaza Pelangi and KSL City, one of the city's busiest retail strips.

tour.title: AEON, IKEA and Toppen
tour.body: The big-box cluster on Jalan Tebrau. In our first draft the line ended here. Now it keeps going.

tour.title: Straight on to Ulu Tiram
tour.body: The line follows Federal Route 3, Jalan Kota Tinggi, for about 7 km to the town of Ulu Tiram, 19 km along the line from Bukit Chagar.
